channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: PL dos Minerais Críticos deve ser apensado para acelerar o trâmite
item.description: The Critical Minerals Bill, approved in the Chamber of Deputies and stalled in the Senate by Davi Alcolumbre, is set to be attached to an older bill in the Infrastructure Committee to speed up its processing, following realignment between Senate leadership and the Lula government. The bill distinguishes critical from strategic minerals, creates the CMCE to review international agreements posing national security risks, and is part of the federal government’s sovereignty strategy amid tensions with the United States.

item.title: Campanha começa neste domingo. Veja o que é permitido até 4 de outubro
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian electoral campaign officially begins on Sunday, August 16, allowing explicit vote requests, live streams, rallies, and paid press and internet advertising until October 2. Rules set by the TSE aim to ensure fairness, following the close of candidate registration at 7 p.m. on Saturday, August 15. Paid online content boosting is permitted until October 1, but officials including the president and heads of Congress and the Supreme Court are barred from using broadcast networks for political propaganda or attacks on parties.

item.title: Lula e Flávio iniciam campanha com corrida eleitoral acirrada
item.description: The 2026 presidential race between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is extremely tight, with recent polls showing a technical tie or minimal lead for Lula, contrasting sharply with his large advantage over Jair Bolsonaro in 2022. Latest surveys from Quaest, Datafolha, and CNT/MDA reveal fluctuating leads, with differences of 3 to 9 percentage points in a potential runoff — all within or near the margin of error. This closeness reflects a more polarized and unpredictable political landscape than in previous elections.

item.title: Candidatos dão a largada na corrida presidencial neste domingo (16/8)
item.description: Presidential candidates launched their campaigns on Sunday (August 16), with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) starting in São Bernardo do Campo (SP), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) on Copacabana Beach (RJ), and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Romeu Zema (Novo), and Renan Santos (Missão) also choosing their political strongholds to begin the race, following TSE authorization for street and online electoral propaganda.

item.title: Campanha de Renan diz ter R$ 2 milhões de vaquinha e venda de livro
item.description: Renan Santos' (Missão) campaign claims to have raised R$ 2 million for his 2026 presidential bid, sourced from an online fundraiser (R$ 1.3 million) and sales of the 'Yellow Book' (R$ 1 million). Inspired by Javier Milei's ultraliberalism, the campaign relies on MBL volunteers, avoids professional consultants, uses commercial flights, and expects up to R$ 3 million more from the Electoral Fund — to be shared among gubernatorial, congressional, and senatorial candidates.

item.title: Flávio fecha acordo com autor de deepfakes que o associavam a Hitler
item.description: Influencer Roger Prado da Fonseca reached an agreement with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a 2026 presidential pre-candidate, after publishing three false deepfakes linking him to Hitler, stealing from retirees, and corruption. The deal requires a public apology on Instagram for at least ten days and payment of five minimum wages in 12 installments to a social entity designated by the court, plus a ban on further offensive posts.

item.title: Admar Gonzaga, advogado de Garotinho, votou pela inelegibilidade dele no TSE
item.description: Admar Gonzaga, current lawyer for Anthony Garotinho, voted for his ineligibility at the TSE in 2018 while serving as a minister. Garotinho was convicted of administrative improbity in the diversion of R$234.3 million in the 'Saúde em Movimento' project, with the conviction becoming final in August 2018 and political rights suspended until August 2026. Gonzaga's defense claims the penalty has already been served, despite a recent TJ-RJ ruling ordering full compliance with the sentence.

item.title: Flávio abre campanha com foco em segurança e pede votos para o Senado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) launched his presidential campaign with a live broadcast, criticizing the PT and Lula’s government, and presented proposals on security, economy, and education. He urged votes for PL-backed candidates in the states, aiming to secure a Senate majority, as 54 of 81 seats are up for election. The campaign officially began Sunday with an event in Copacabana, electoral propaganda is now authorized, and the first round is set for October 4, 2026.

item.title: Entrevista: 'Classe C não enxerga Lula ou Flávio como passaporte para futuro melhor', diz presidente do Locomotiva
item.description: Renato Meirelles states that Brazil's C class — representing 53% of the population with an average income of R$3,500 — lost political connection after 2013, when the 'decade of optimism' ended. Despite benefiting from policies like minimum wage increases and formal employment, this group believes its progress came from individual effort, not government action, and no longer sees Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro as symbols of a better future. The sense of stagnation has fueled an anti-system sentiment, as the C class blames the government for failing to meet expectations it helped create.

item.title: Tema central na campanha que começa hoje, medo de ser assaltado alcança dois a cada três eleitores, aponta pesquisa
item.description: The Ideia poll reveals that 66% of Brazilians fear or greatly fear being victim of an armed robbery, and 63.9% fear having their cellphone stolen, making insecurity a central theme in the 2026 electoral campaign, cited by candidates across the political spectrum. The data, obtained exclusively by GLOBO, shows that the sense of insecurity affects the majority of the population.

item.title: Violência pauta voto para presidente de 63% dos eleitores de direita, contra 45% à esquerda, revela pesquisa Ideia
item.description: The Ideia poll shows public safety is a priority for 45.7% of voters in the presidential race, but with strong polarization: 63.7% of Bolsonarist right-wing voters consider it crucial for their presidential vote, compared to only 45.6% of non-Lulist left-wing voters. Conversely, for state governments, non-Lulist left-wing voters prioritize security in 62.2% of cases, while Bolsonarist right-wing voters do so in 44.6%, indicating a perceived inversion of responsibility across government levels.

item.title: Lula 'farmando aura': aos 80 anos, petista tenta rejuvenescer imagem para atrair eleitorado mais jovem
item.description: Lula's re-election campaign, at age 80, is attempting to rejuvenate his image by adopting youth-associated language, gestures, and social media trends—such as gaming slang, K-pop hand signs, and TikTok content—to appeal to younger voters and counter perceptions of political fatigue. The strategy includes portraying him as a 'friend of millennials,' emphasizing his 1970s union activism as anti-establishment symbolism, and highlighting his gym routine and whey protein use to convey vitality. The campaign launch at Vila Euclides Stadium in São Bernardo do Campo features archival footage of Lula leading strikes in the ABC region to reinforce this narrative.

item.title: Em meio a incômodo com desempenho nas redes, Flávio Bolsonaro escala aliados para alavancar presença digital
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign is seeking to boost its digital presence by mobilizing allies to counter attacks and amplify messages, reducing his personal reliance on social media. This strategy arises from his low engagement compared to Michelle Bolsonaro, whose video received nearly eight times more views. Despite the strong online presence of the far right, Flávio's campaign struggles to convert the accumulated digital capital of Bolsonarism into effective support for his candidacy.

item.title: Renan Santos escolhe SP, palco que projetou MBL, para lançar campanha
item.description: Renan Santos, former founder of the MBL, officially launches his presidential campaign for the Partido Missão in an event at Largo São Francisco, São Paulo, featuring speeches by Amanda Vettorazzo, Kim Kataguiri, and Aroldo Medina. The event, scheduled for Sunday (August 16), is expected to gather around 2,000 people, highlighting his opposition to the PT and advocacy for liberal economic policies. His campaign includes criticism of the Lula government and a proposal to involve the Federal Police in investigating alleged electoral irregularities.

item.title: Vox: Marina, Tebet e André do Prado lideram corrida ao Senado em SP
item.description: Marina Silva (Rede) leads the Senate race in São Paulo with 26.1% of voting intentions, followed by Simone Tebet (MDB) at 25.5% and André do Prado (PL) at 21.5%, according to a Vox Brasil Institute poll. With a 2.55-point margin of error and 53.9% of voters undecided, the race remains highly open and competitive.

item.title: Vox: Tarcísio tem 53,7% e Haddad, 34% no 1º turno em São Paulo
item.description: The Vox Brasil poll shows Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leading with 53.7% of voting intentions and Fernando Haddad (PT) at 34% in the first round for São Paulo governor, suggesting a likely first-round victory even accounting for the 2.55-point margin of error. In the second round, Tarcísio holds 54.3% against Haddad's 35.2%, and in valid votes reaches 60.7% versus Haddad's 39.3%. Tarcísio has 66.5% approval and 22.3% rejection, while Haddad has 46.1% rejection.

item.title: Caiado compra fazendas, encontra posseiros e agora briga na Justiça para recuperar dinheiro
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) is legally challenging the purchase of Fazenda Pedras, occupied by squatters since 2002, after discovering the property was under illegal occupation. He seeks the return of over R$ 3 million paid for the land, claiming contractual breach by the seller. In first instance, the TJGO annulled the transaction only for this farm and ordered restitution of the paid amounts, updated for inflation.

item.title: "Onde tudo começou": Lula lança campanha em SP neste domingo (15/8)
item.description: Lula launched his re-election campaign in São Bernardo do Campo, SP, under the slogan 'Where it all began', returning to his union roots from the 1980s. The event marked the official start of electoral campaigns in Brazil and featured support from allied parties including PSB, PCdoB, PV, PDT, PSol and Rede, alongside Vice President Geraldo Alckmin. The strategy aims to strengthen the PT in Brazil's largest electoral college, overcoming historical resistance to the party in São Paulo.

item.title: Manchester City e Arsenal lutam pelo título da Supercopa da Inglaterra
item.description: Arsenal and Manchester City are set to clash in the English Super Cup on Sunday (August 16) at Principality Stadium in Wales at 11 a.m. Brasília time. The match features the Premier League champions (Arsenal) against the FA Cup winners (Manchester City), with both teams aiming to add another trophy to their collection. Arsenal seeks its 18th title, while City aims for an eighth, having won the 2024 edition against Manchester United on penalties.

item.title: Brasil y México plantan cara a la hostilidad y las injerencias de Trump y las derechas latinoamericanas
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum are strengthening cooperation between Brazil and Mexico in response to perceived U.S. influence and the rise of reactionary forces in Latin America. Both leaders emphasized the strategic importance of bilateral ties, with Lula highlighting collaboration and Sheinbaum underscoring growing trade and diplomatic relations. The meeting reflects a joint resistance to Trump-era policies and the advancement of right-wing movements across the region.

item.title: Lula e Flávio escolhem redutos seguros para começar campanha
item.description: Lula (PT) officially launches his campaign in São Bernardo do Campo, the historic heartland of Brazilian unionism and the PT, at 9 a.m., while Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) chooses Copacabana Beach in Rio de Janeiro, starting at 10 a.m., for his debut. Both selections carry symbolic weight: Lula emphasizes his working-class roots, and Flávio seeks to solidify Bolsonaro’s base in the Southeast.

item.title: TSE recebe 13 registros de candidaturas à Presidência. Veja quem são
item.description: The TSE received 13 presidential candidacy registration requests for the 2026 elections, with the deadline closing at 7 p.m. on Saturday (August 15). The last registration was Pablo Marçal (PRTB), who, despite being ineligible until 2032 due to TRE-SP convictions, obtained a provisional injunction recognizing his party affiliation, allowing the filing. Campaigning officially begins Sunday (August 16), with the first round set for October 4 and a potential runoff on October 25.

item.title: Campanha eleitoral começa neste domingo; entenda o que muda e o que os candidatos podem fazer agora
item.description: The 2026 electoral campaign officially begins this Sunday, allowing candidates to conduct street, internet, and graphic propaganda, with TV and radio ads restricted until August 28. Leading presidential candidates — Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Renan Santos, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema — launched their campaigns in their political strongholds, emphasizing personal and regional symbolism. Social media promotion is permitted, including paid boosting, but only to support one's own candidacy, not to amplify attacks on opponents.

item.title: Inelegível até 2032, Pablo Marçal é lançado como candidato à Presidência pelo PRTB
item.description: The PRTB filed Pablo Marçal's presidential candidacy for 2026, despite his ineligibility until 2032 due to a 2024 conviction for improper use of communication media during his São Paulo mayoral campaign. A court order allowed his party switch from União Brasil to PRTB, but the TSE will review the registration, with likely challenges from the Electoral Prosecutor's Office and opponents.

item.title: Saiba quem são os candidatos ao governo do Paraná
item.description: In the 2026 elections, Paraná will have eight candidates for governor, with Sergio Moro (PL) leading the stimulated poll at 40.2% of voting intentions, followed by Sandro Alex (PSD) at 24.8% and Requião Filho (PDT) at 21%. The margin of error is 2.67 percentage points. The state has 8.61 million voters, making it the fifth-largest electoral college in Brazil.

item.title: Mudanças no Nordeste e direita competitiva testam solidez do eleitorado lulista
item.description: The article describes the tradition of the Vaqueiro's Mass in Serrita, Pernambuco, highlighting the participation of cowboys and local residents in a religious and cultural event of the sertão. The setting reflects the rural identity and popular practices of the Brazilian Northeast, without direct mention of candidates or electoral debates.

item.title: Justiça Eleitoral concede liminar e Marçal protocola pedido de registro de candidatura à Presidência
item.description: The Electoral Justice of São Paulo granted a preliminary injunction allowing influencer Pablo Marçal to change parties and affiliate with the PRTB, enabling him to file his presidential candidacy registration for 2026. However, his eight-year ineligibility, upheld by the TRE-SP for improper use of social media during the 2024 São Paulo mayoral campaign, remains in place and must be overturned for him to run. The ruling is provisional and subject to appeal, with Marçal’s defense preparing to challenge it before the TSE.

item.title: Saiba quem são os candidatos ao governo de Santa Catarina em 2026
item.description: Santa Catarina will have 8 gubernatorial candidates in 2026, with Jorginho Mello (PL) leading the race at 52.8% voter intention, followed by João Rodrigues (PSD) at 20.3%. The registration deadline was August 15, 2026, though candidacies remain subject to judicial challenges. Information is available through the TSE and Poder360’s Políticos do Brasil and Poder Drive platforms.

item.title: JHC confirma candidatura ao governo e evita embate com Lira em Alagoas
item.description: Former Maceió mayor João Henrique Caldas (JHC, PSDB) confirmed his candidacy for governor of Alagoas in 2026, avoiding a direct confrontation with Arthur Lira (PP) by abandoning a Senate run. His decision follows rapprochement with the Lula government, including personal meetings and support for his aunt’s STJ nomination. JHC will now face Renan Filho (MDB) in a tight race, with polls showing a technical tie at 46% each, as he seeks to consolidate right-wing support without splitting the Bolsonarist vote.

item.title: Saiba quem são os candidatos ao Senado por Rondônia em 2026
item.description: Rondônia will have 10 Senate candidates in the 2026 elections, with registration closing on August 15. A Real Time Big Data poll from July 15 shows Fernando Máximo (PL) leading with 19% voter intention, followed by Sílvia Cristina (PP) at 14%. The state has 1.27 million voters and is contesting two Senate seats.

item.title: Inelegível, Pablo Marçal registra candidatura a presidente pelo PRTB
item.description: Pablo Marçal's presidential candidacy for the 2026 elections was registered by the PRTB following a judicial injunction that regularized his party affiliation, despite his ineligibility. The registration was submitted to the TSE system but still requires final approval from the electoral court.

item.title: O verdadeiro motivo de Tereza Cristina não ter virado vice de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Ciro Nogueira, president of the PP, initially backed Tereza Cristina as a potential running mate for Flávio Bolsonaro but withdrew support after Federal Police investigations linked his allies to money laundering schemes involving banker Daniel Vorcaro, fearing police embarrassment before the election. He chose not to take the risk, despite having previously considered Nogueira as a likely vice and having given Tereza Cristina permission to seek internal party support.

item.title: Caiado descarta apoio a Lula no 2º turno após fala de Kassab
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, the PSD presidential candidate, ruled out any support for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in a potential runoff, reinforcing his long-standing opposition to the Workers' Party and stating his candidacy aims to remove the PT from power. The statement followed remarks by his running mate, Gilberto Kassab, who claimed Centrão parties are effectively aligned with Lula’s re-election. Caiado stressed there is no scenario in which he would support Lula, citing his four-decade political record, including leading the impeachment of Dilma Rousseff and reducing homicide rates in Goiás without leaving debt.

item.title: PRTB lança Pablo Marçal, que está inelegível, como candidato à Presidência
item.description: The PRTB filed Pablo Marçal's candidacy for President of Brazil, despite his legal ineligibility under electoral law. The party claims it obtained judicial authorization for his affiliation, but Marçal’s ineligibility remains a substantive barrier to his campaign. The move has sparked controversy, as Brazilian law prohibits individuals with final convictions or other disqualifying conditions from running for elected office.

item.title: Pablo Marçal, que está inelegível, registra candidatura à Presidência
item.description: Pablo Marçal, the PRTB candidate who is currently ineligible, registered his presidential candidacy with the TSE following a provisional injunction that allowed his temporary affiliation with the party. The registration took place on Saturday (August 15) and marks a twist in the presidential race, as his ineligibility remains under judicial review.

item.title: Ao conquistar os líderes do Centrão, um a um, risco de Lula é um novo ‘petrolão’
item.description: By securing support from Centrão figures such as Ciro Nogueira, Davi Alcolumbre, and Hugo Motta, President Lula strengthens his congressional base and re-election prospects in 2026, yet repeats the pattern that led to the mensalão and Petrolão scandals. This pragmatic, non-ideological alliance strategy involves concessions to regional and sectoral interests, risking quid-pro-quo arrangements that could compromise Petrobras and governance. The cost, the text argues, is borne by society, reviving a cycle of institutional corruption in the name of political survival.

item.title: 49,9% dos candidatos de 2026 se declaram negros; 48,6%, brancos
item.description: In the 2026 elections, 49.9% of the 10,200 candidates self-declared as Black, representing a 0.4 percentage point decrease from the 50.3% recorded in 2022. The figure includes 7,412 pardos (mixed-race) and 2,788 pretos (Black) candidates, based on preliminary TSE data released after the August 15, 2026 registration deadline. Despite the decline, the policy requiring parties to allocate at least 30% of campaign funds to Black and mixed-race candidatures remains in effect since 2024.

item.title: Candidaturas femininas são 34,8% nas Eleições de 2026
item.description: Women account for 34.8% of candidacies in Brazil's 2026 General Elections, a new proportional record, up one percentage point from the 2022 presidential election. In absolute numbers, there will be 13,320 male candidates and 7,116 female candidates, despite women comprising 51.5% of Brazil's population according to the 2022 IBGE Census.

item.title: Saiba quem são os candidatos ao governo de São Paulo em 2026
item.description: São Paulo will have 7 candidates for governor in 2026, with Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) seeking re-election and Fernando Haddad (PT) as his main rival. A Meio/Ideia poll from August 10 shows Tarcísio leading with 51% voting intention, compared to Haddad's 34%, suggesting a potential first-round victory. Candidate registration closed on August 15, 2026, and candidate data is publicly accessible via Políticos do Brasil and Poder Drive.

item.title: Rui Costa Pimenta declara ao TSE não possuir bens
item.description: Rui Costa Pimenta, presidential candidate for the PCO, declared to the TSE that he owns no assets when registering his candidacy. Hertz Dias of the PSTU made the same declaration. Asset disclosure is mandatory for candidacy registration and aims to ensure transparency.

item.title: Caiado diz que não apoiará Lula após fala de Kassab sobre Centrão
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) stated he will not support Lula in any electoral scenario, emphasizing his historical opposition to the PT since 1989. The declaration followed criticism from his running mate, Gilberto Kassab (PSD), who claimed the Centrão is not neutral and backs Lula’s re-election, while calling Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL) chances 'zero'. Caiado said his campaign aims to remove the PT from power and position itself as a right-wing alternative independent of Bolsonarism.

item.title: Vanderlan Cardoso (PSD) declara patrimônio de R$ 66 milhões; veja patrimônio de candidato ao Senado em Goiás
item.description: PSD Senate candidate Vanderlan Cardoso from Goiás declared R$ 66.8 million in assets to the TSE, with major holdings including private credit (R$ 24.5 million), aircraft shares (R$ 13.3 million), and an R$ 8.3 million residence. This reflects a 149.28% increase from his 2024 mayoral candidacy in Goiânia, when he declared R$ 26.8 million. The disclosure highlights significant wealth concentration in financial and high-value real assets.

item.title: Justiça proíbe suspeito de se aproximar de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A court in Minas Gerais barred a suspect accused of threatening Senator Flávio Bolsonaro from coming within 500 meters of the lawmaker, his residence, workplace, and campaign activities. The restraining order was issued following an investigation into threats against the presidential candidate.

item.title: Polícia do Senado identifica suspeito de ameaçar Flávio em Minas
item.description: The Senate Legislative Police and Minas Gerais Civil Police executed a search and seizure warrant in Juiz de Fora (MG) against a man suspected of threatening presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro with violent Facebook comments. The suspect, who has eight prior records for assault and threats, was taken in for questioning, had electronic devices seized, and was barred from coming within 500 meters of the candidate. The operation takes place amid heightened alert, as Juiz de Fora was the site of the knife attack on Jair Bolsonaro in 2018.

item.title: Lula prepara ato de campanha com slogan “O Brasil pronto pra mais”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will launch his 2026 re-election campaign on August 16, 2026, at 9 a.m., at the Estádio 1º de Maio in São Bernardo do Campo (SP), unveiling the slogan 'Brazil ready for more'. The event, expected to draw 20,000 attendees, will highlight government achievements in social programs, national defense, rare earth exploration, and full-time education, while attacking PL candidate Flávio Bolsonaro for alleged alignment with Donald Trump.

item.title: Presidenciáveis declaram patrimônios de R$ 33 mil a R$ 242 milhões
item.description: Presidential candidates in Brazil's 2026 election declared assets ranging from R$33,000 to R$242.2 million, according to TSE data. Augusto Cury (Avante) leads with R$242.2 million, followed by Romeu Zema (Novo) at R$178.7 million and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) at R$52.5 million. Hertz Dias (PSTU) and Rui Costa Pimenta (PCO) declared no assets.

item.title: Candidato do PCB à Presidência declara R$ 454,5 mil em bens
item.description: PCB presidential candidate Edmilson Costa declared R$ 454,485.68 in assets to the TSE, a 9.5% decrease from 2014 when he ran for Senate. His running mate, Cleusa Santos, reported R$ 1.79 million, a 16.2% increase from 2024. The figures come from the DivulgaCandContas system, with candidate registration closing on Saturday (Aug 15, 2026).

item.title: Polícia do Senado cumpre mandado contra suspeito de ameaçar Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Senate Police executed a search and seizure warrant in Juiz de Fora (MG) against a suspect accused of threatening Senator Flávio Bolsonaro on social media. The threat was identified by the Senate’s Intelligence Situation Room during monitoring of risks to campaigning legislators. The suspect gave testimony, seized materials will undergo forensic analysis, and the case has been referred to the Minas Gerais Public Prosecutor’s Office.

item.title: Campanha presidencial pega fogo, mas ainda não comove os eleitores
item.description: The 2026 presidential race is fiercely contested between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, with both technically tied in second-round simulations (43% to 40%), despite scandals involving the Master Bank scheme and alleged looting of INSS pension funds. Despite high media coverage, most voters remain disengaged: 51% do not name a candidate spontaneously, 41% are unaware of the Bolsonaro family reconciliation, and 29% of independents say they will not vote.

item.title: Tatuador é detido suspeito de ameaçar esfaquear Flávio em Juiz de Fora (MG)
item.description: Lauro Cesar Costa Junior, a 41-year-old tattoo artist, was detained in Juiz de Fora (MG) on suspicion of threatening to stab Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), who has a scheduled agenda in the city next Monday. The incident occurred in the same municipality where Jair Bolsonaro was stabbed during the 2018 election campaign. Authorities are investigating the motive and credibility of the threat.
